newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market closed on Monday with strong gains, supported by a stronger peseta and by a rebounding Italian market.
But traders expected a touch of profit taking on Tuesday and Wednesday ahead of Spain's public holidays on Thursday and Friday. A flurry of U.S. data this week also put the market on the edge.
"I do not see our market gaining more than that. There's virtually no market," said a dealer at ABN Amro in Madrid.
He added that the long-term future offered strong resistance at around 113.20. It closed on Monday at 113.19.
"Peripheral markets outperformed German Bunds today because of the dollar. But I do not expect any major movement until the U.S. data is out," said a Madrid-based dealer.
Dealers remained positive on the outlook for the short end, with the market expecting the Bank of Spain to soon cut its official money market rate once more.
A stronger peseta, trading late on Monday at around 84.28/30 per mark versus 84.33/35 on Friday, supported the view of a possible easing in the second half of May, dealers said.
